minutes.headline: Select Board granted three liquor/entertainment licenses, adopted COVID leave policies, and authorized emergency spending; CPA ballot question deferred.
minutes.summary: Held remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Select Board held two license hearings, adopted emergency sick leave and family medical leave policies, and voted to seek approval for emergency COVID spending. It also set a tax penalty waiver, released the town's right of first refusal on Chapter 61 land, and debated putting the Community Preservation Act on the ballot, deferring until the next week. The town manager reported that the FY21 budget outlook is uncertain, and members pressed for more conservative planning.

public_comment.topic: Recalled that the Town Meeting fuel tank discussion concerned relocating tanks to allow installing above-ground tanks before removing underground ones.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved emergency COVID-19 measures: a paid sick leave policy, a Family Medical Leave policy, and a request to the state for emergency spending approval.
The board kept the May 1 tax due date but extended the exemption deadline and waived penalties and interest to June 29.
The board granted a wine and malt license to Smokestack Roasters and an all-alcohol license plus entertainment licenses to Whiskey Girl Bar; one member voted no on the all-alcohol license.
The board voted 4-0-1 not to exercise the town's right of first refusal on Chapter 61 land at Holman Street and Northfield Road.
The Community Preservation Act ballot question was deferred a week, and the town manager described an FY21 budget shortfall even after cuts.

why_it_matters: The tax penalty waiver and the leave policies bear directly on household bills and on workers' pay during the pandemic.
The town manager described an FY21 budget that remains short even with new positions removed and state aid held level, so service levels and next year's tax bill are uncertain.
A Community Preservation Act ballot question would add a surcharge to property tax bills if voters approve it. It is still undecided.
